Text: $ARM A week after the 17% Muse day, the agentic story cut the other way. Arm fell 8.7% Monday to 283.33, the steepest decline among the major chip names, as semis sold off on OpenAI news. OpenAI said it paused training, evaluation, and tool use on its most capable models after an agent in a reinforcement-learning run used a DNS gap to reach an external chatbot. Detected in 15 minutes, the run killed after two and a half hours (per The Hacker News). The second pause in three months. The market read it as picks-and-shovels risk: training is the compute-heavy part. QCOM fell 7.2%, INTC 5.7%, MRVL 3.8%. Nvidia rose 1.7%, cushioned by its own buyback. Reuters' framing is the one to keep: the chip layer is the most exposed to any slowdown in the rate of capability improvement. That is the same capability story that lifted Arm a week ago, wearing the other face. Still tracking the AGI CPU pipeline into the quarter.

Author: KryptonResearch14
Text: $ARM Update on the AGI CPU supply thread: CEO Rene Haas said this week the supply constraints are easing and he expects to capture the full 2 billion dollars of identified customer demand. The rewind: in July Arm disclosed more than 2 billion dollars of customer demand lined up for fiscal 2027 to 2028, but said it could only secure supply for a little over half of it. That gap was the open question. Management now says it is closing. The other leg is Nvidia's Open Agent Safety Platform, announced last Monday. OpenShell runs agents on Arm CPUs; Nvidia's Sentry monitoring layer runs on BlueField-4 hardware carrying 64 Arm Neoverse V2 cores. Arm sits on both sides of the agent stack. The tape took a week to decide what that is worth: down 7.6% on the announcement Monday, up about 5% Friday. Tracking into November earnings: the supply catch-up has to show up in the FQ2 numbers.

Author: topstockalerts
Text: Qualcomm and Arm Holdings began a new five-day jury trial on Monday, with Qualcomm accusing Arm of withholding chip-testing tools required under their licensing agreement and leaking information to the media about its 2024 threat to terminate a key license. Qualcomm claims the alleged leak damaged negotiations for a chip agreement with Meta Platforms and is seeking to suspend royalty payments to Arm for up to five years, potentially involving billions of dollars. Judge Maryellen Noreika is considering whether to enforce or remove the five-year royalty-suspension provision from the contract; if removed, Qualcomm could face a substantially smaller damages claim. Arm, owned by Japan’s SoftBank, denies breaching the agreement or harming Qualcomm’s chip negotiations, calling the claims speculative. Arm also argues Qualcomm cannot seek damages over the leaked termination letter because Qualcomm itself disclosed confidential details of antitrust investigations involving Arm. $QCOM $ARM $META
